name: granite41-3b-german-tutor-v4-4bit
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from ibm-granite/granite-4.1-3b (config.json max_position_embeddings 131072). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: Inherited unchanged from ibm-granite/granite-4.1-3b: 40 full GQA layers (kv heads 8, head_dim 64) and 0 other layers, per the base config.json.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-03. A finetune of ibm-granite/granite-4.1-3b, not a new base model: same config.json, same 3.403 parameters . Recorded as a contender because it publishes benchmark evidence against its own base; the evidence rows below are card-sourced and marked vendor_claim. Licence apache-2.0, repo created 2026-08-19. CAVEAT: the repo ships 4-bit MLX weights only (group size 64, affine), not bf16. The card presents those weights as the model rather than as a quantisation test, so the rows are the shipped model's numbers, but no bf16-vs-4bit ablation is published. All four rows are the author's own German-grammar suites (203 items total, teacher-generated and LanguageTool/spaCy-validated) scored under an app-guard convention - a reply counts only if the app's parser would show it to the learner - so they measure tutor-app usefulness, not general capability and not a public benchmark. Against its own 3.3 sibling on identical items the paired result is 26 gained / 15 lost (exact McNemar p = 0.12), i.e. not significant; the model trades a 43% miss rate for a 25% miss rate at a 9% false-correction rate.
